name: APT41 – APT Threat Map
description: Técnicas de APT41 com cobertura do catálogo (score 3=regra, 2=parcial, 1=lacuna)

techniques.comment: APT41 has used hashdump, Mimikatz, Procdump, and the Windows Credential Editor to dump password hashes from memory and authenticate to other user accounts. | cobertura: regra

APT41 extracted user account data from the Security Account Managerr (SAM), making a copy of this database from the registry using the `reg save` command or by exploiting volume shadow copies. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used ntdsutil to obtain a copy of the victim environment `ntds.dit` file. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has uploaded files and data from a compromised host. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used the Steam community page as a fallback mechanism for C2. | cobertura: regra
APT41 queried registry values to determine items such as configured RDP ports and network configurations. | cobertura: regra
APT41 deployed rootkits on Linux systems. | cobertura: regra
APT41 collected MAC addresses from victim machines. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has used MiPing to discover active systems in the victim network. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used RDP for lateral movement. APT41 used NATBypass to expose local RDP ports on compromised systems to the Internet. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has transferred implant files using Windows Admin Shares and the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol, then executes files through Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI). | cobertura: regra
APT41 used VMProtected binaries in multiple intrusions. | cobertura: regra
APT41 uses packers such as Themida to obfuscate malicious files. | cobertura: regra
APT41 transfers post-exploitation files dividing the payload into fixed-size chunks to evade detection. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has executed `whoami` commands, including using the WMIEXEC utility to execute this on remote machines. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has created services to appear as benign system tools. | cobertura: regra
APT41 attempted to masquerade their files as popular anti-virus software. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used a hidden shell script in `/etc/rc.d/init.d` to leverage the `ADORE.XSEC`backdoor and `Adore-NG` rootkit. | cobertura: parcial (ASR/D3FEND)
APT41 used a malware variant called WIDETONE to conduct port scans on specified subnets. | cobertura: regra

APT41 used WMI in several ways, including for execution of commands via WMIEXEC as well as for persistence via PowerSploit. APT41 has executed files through Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI). | cobertura: regra

APT41 has enumerated IP addresses of network resources and used the `netstat` command as part of network reconnaissance. The group has also used a malware variant, HIGHNOON, to enumerate active RDP sessions. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used a compromised account to create a scheduled task on a system. | cobertura: regra
APT41 malware TIDYELF loaded the main WINTERLOVE component by injecting it into the iexplore.exe process. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used a keylogger called GEARSHIFT on a target system. | cobertura: regra
APT41 leveraged PowerShell to deploy malware families in victims’ environments. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used `cmd.exe /c` to execute commands on remote machines. APT41 used a batch file to install persistence for the Cobalt Strike BEACON loader. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used Linux shell commands for system survey and information gathering prior to exploitation of vulnerabilities such as CVE-2019-19871. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used `net group` commands to enumerate various Windows user groups and permissions. | cobertura: regra
APT41 attempted to remove evidence of some of its activity by deleting Bash histories. | cobertura: regra
APT41 deleted files from the system. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used HTTP to download payloads for CVE-2019-19781 and CVE-2020-10189 exploits. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used exploit payloads that initiate download via ftp. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used DNS for C2 communications. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used compromised credentials to log on to other systems. | cobertura: regra
APT41 uses multiple built-in commands such as `systeminfo` and `net config Workstation` to enumerate victim system basic configuration information. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has executed `file /bin/pwd` on exploited victims, perhaps to return architecture related information. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used built-in `net` commands to enumerate local administrator groups. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used built-in `net` commands to enumerate domain administrator users. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used a tool called CLASSFON to covertly proxy network communications. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has added user accounts to the User and Admin groups. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used legitimate websites for C2 through dead drop resolvers (DDR), including GitHub, Pastebin, and Microsoft TechNet. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used the storescyncsvc.dll BEACON backdoor to download a secondary backdoor. | cobertura: parcial (ASR/D3FEND)

APT41 used certutil to download additional files. APT41 downloaded post-exploitation tools such as Cobalt Strike via command shell following initial access. APT41 has uploaded Procdump and NATBypass to a staging directory and has used these tools in follow-on activities. | cobertura: regra
APT41 performed password brute-force attacks on the local admin account. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used a malware variant called GOODLUCK to modify the registry in order to steal credentials. | cobertura: regra
APT41 compromised an online billing/payment service using VPN access between a third-party service provider and the targeted payment service. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used the `net share` command as part of network reconnaissance. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has created user accounts. | cobertura: regra

APT41 exploited CVE-2020-10189 against Zoho ManageEngine Desktop Central through unsafe deserialization, and CVE-2019-19781 to compromise Citrix Application Delivery Controllers (ADC) and gateway devices. APT41 leveraged vulnerabilities such as ProxyLogon exploitation or SQL injection for initial access. APT41 exploited CVE-2021-26855 against a vulnerable… | cobertura: regra
APT41 gained access to production environments where they could inject malicious code into legitimate, signed files and widely distribute them to end users. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used BITSAdmin to download and install payloads. | cobertura: regra
APT41 leveraged the follow exploits in their operations: CVE-2012-0158, CVE-2015-1641, CVE-2017-0199, CVE-2017-11882, and CVE-2019-3396. | cobertura: regra
APT41 cloned victim user Git repositories during intrusions. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used compiled HTML (.chm) files for targeting. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has used rundll32.exe to execute a loader. | cobertura: regra

APT41 has encrypted payloads using the Data Protection API (DPAPI), which relies on keys tied to specific user accounts on specific machines. APT41 has also environmentally keyed second stage malware with an RC5 key derived in part from the infected system's volume serial number. | cobertura: lacuna
APT41 used scheduled tasks created via Group Policy Objects (GPOs) to deploy ransomware. | cobertura: regra

APT41 used a ransomware called Encryptor RaaS to encrypt files on the targeted systems and provide a ransom note to the user. APT41 also used Microsoft Bitlocker to encrypt workstations and Jetico’s BestCrypt to encrypt servers. | cobertura: regra
APT41 deployed a Monero cryptocurrency mining tool in a victim’s environment. | cobertura: regra
APT41 deployed Master Boot Record bootkits on Windows systems to hide their malware and maintain persistence on victim systems. | cobertura: regra
APT41 modified legitimate Windows services to install malware backdoors. APT41 created the StorSyncSvc service to provide persistence for Cobalt Strike. | cobertura: regra
APT41 leveraged sticky keys to establish persistence. | cobertura: regra

APT41 created and modified startup files for persistence. APT41 added a registry key in `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Svchost` to establish persistence for Cobalt Strike. | cobertura: regra
APT41 uses tools such as Mimikatz to enable lateral movement via captured password hashes. | cobertura: regra
APT41 leveraged code-signing certificates to sign malware when targeting both gaming and non-gaming organizations. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has obtained information about accounts, lists of employees, and plaintext and hashed passwords from databases. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used BrowserGhost, a tool designed to obtain credentials from browsers, to retrieve information from password stores. | cobertura: regra

APT41 created a RAR archive of targeted files for exfiltration. Additionally, APT41 used the makecab.exe utility to both download tools, such as NATBypass, to the victim network and to archive a file for exfiltration. | cobertura: regra
APT41 sent spearphishing emails with attachments such as compiled HTML (.chm) files to initially compromise their victims. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has used DGAs to change their C2 servers monthly. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used svchost.exe and Net to execute a system service installed to launch a Cobalt Strike BEACON loader. | cobertura: regra
APT41 uses remote shares to move and remotely execute payloads during lateral movemement. | cobertura: regra

APT41 has used search order hijacking to execute malicious payloads, such as Winnti for Windows. APT41 has also used legitimate executables to perform DLL side-loading of their malware. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has configured payloads to load via LD_PRELOAD. | cobertura: regra
APT41 has obtained and used tools such as Mimikatz, pwdump, PowerSploit, and Windows Credential Editor. | cobertura: regra
APT41 used the Acunetix SQL injection vulnerability scanner in target reconnaissance operations, as well as the JexBoss tool to identify vulnerabilities in Java applications. | cobertura: regra
APT41 leverages various tools and frameworks to brute-force directories on web servers. | cobertura: regra
APT41 uses the Chinese website fofa.su, similar to the Shodan scanning service, for passive scanning of victims. | cobertura: lacuna
APT41 used `NATBypass` to bypass firewall restrictions and to access compromised systems via RDP. | cobertura: lacuna
APT41 impersonated an employee at a video game developer company to send phishing emails. | cobertura: lacuna
APT41 developed a custom injector that enables an Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) bypass, making malicious processes invisible to Windows logging. | cobertura: regra
APT41 attempted to remove evidence of some of its activity by clearing Windows security and system events. | cobertura: regra
